lead_headline: Restaurant tracker enters day two of total silence—zero new leads detected across all metro channels as Memorial Day freeze persists

restaurant.blurb: Zero new leads today—complete detection blackout continues from Monday as post-holiday dormancy extends into Tuesday. Active pipeline holds at 188 total (106 openings, 82 closures).

liquor.blurb: Day 26 of total regulatory shutdown—Colorado's liquor licensing system remains in complete suspended animation with zero applications filed, zero status updates processed, zero administrative activity recorded since April 30. The database freeze now extends across the entire May calendar as the state's regulatory apparatus maintains absolute paralysis with no official acknowledgment, no contingency protocols, no timeline communicated to licensees whose expansion plans remain indefinitely frozen. All 12,396 tracked licenses locked in bureaucratic stasis as the invisible application backlog compounds behind administrative walls while officials sustain their month-long silence on restoration plans or even basic recognition that normal operations ceased 26 days ago.

reputation.blurb: Three mentions yesterday, maintaining the single-digit daily cadence that has defined the post-Memorial Day period—weekly total climbs to 48 across 10 unique sources, down 14% from prior week's 56 as the holiday weekend suppresses pickup velocity. Instagram commands 19 mentions (40% of weekly volume), Reddit delivers 9, Facebook contributes 6, Denver Post adds 5, Hoodline rounds out the top five with 3. Google News RSS drives 100% of discovery (all 48 mentions). The week-over-week decline reverses the late-May acceleration pattern as Memorial Day weekend creates predictable slowdown in media citation activity, though monthly tracking remains elevated at 213 total mentions as May approaches its final days.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +0 yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) as Memorial Day flatline extends into Tuesday—zero subscriber movement for second consecutive day. MTD holds at +23 (+0.9/day), 90-day net stands at +135. The seven-day window shows net +2 (6 new, 4 canceled) as churn ratio stays favorable but volume remains anemic. Pattern crystallizes: May's concentrated mid-month surge (May 12-15) generated the bulk of monthly progress, then activity collapsed to near-dormant levels through a sustained 12-day drought that now encompasses the holiday weekend and beyond. YTD pace of +1.2/day continues outpacing the sluggish MTD crawl, highlighting how thoroughly momentum evaporated after the brief May spike as daily flow stabilizes at minimal-to-zero levels.
